title: AI Record Producer
teaser: A system prompt that acts as a record producer for AI-generated music, built to cut wasted iterations and protect creative focus.

sections.problem: Suno rewards precise prompting, but "precise" isn't the same as "long." Left unguided, a prompting session drifts in a few predictable ways: elaboration creep, where every generation that doesn't quite land invites one more instruction until the additions start competing instead of adding precision; chasing a moving target, where lyrics and production keep getting rewritten against each other because neither one ever locks first; blaming the wrong layer, where a drifting generation gets patched with a lyric or BPM change when the actual cause is an ambiguous prompt identity upstream; and role confusion, where an AI producer quietly slides into rewriting the song outright and turns a collaborator into a ghostwriter. Underneath all four is the same goal: expedite the outcome. That means lessening the amount of credit waste, and it means the songwriter gets to spend more time on the creative input and enjoying the output, instead of needing to understand every nuance of the system generating it.
sections.build: An AI production partner for a songwriter working in Suno, not a lyric generator or beat maker, but the role that sits between a songwriter's intent and a usable AI-generated track. Built and developed inside Claude, but designed to be platform-agnostic, the underlying reasoning holds regardless of which AI agent is running it. Nine files split what to decide from when to decide it: a session controller that owns sequencing and confirmation gates, and separate modules that each own one kind of judgment, sound identity, rhythm and phrasing, prompt construction, tag syntax, and diagnosing drift. The workflow starts by identifying where the songwriter is actually starting from (an anchor line already written, a reference song, or just a feeling with no fixed target yet), since that single choice changes everything downstream, including whether the production identity should lock before or after the lyrics are finished.
sections.technical: Nine markdown and text files functioning as a modular system prompt, not application code. Built and tested inside a Claude Project's custom instructions and project knowledge, but written to be portable: any AI system that supports a persistent system prompt plus reference files can run it. The Suno-specific knowledge lives in its own module (tag syntax, prompt construction) so the reasoning modules underneath stay usable regardless of which model is driving the conversation.
sections.learning: Splitting what to decide from when to decide it mattered more than any single rule inside either file. Once sequencing had its own dedicated file, the other modules stopped needing to defensively re-explain order to each other. The minimalism principle needed to be a hierarchy, not just a preference, since "shorter is better" isn't actionable on its own; the system had to define what "enough" looks like at each level so every addition beyond it has to justify itself against a specific problem rather than a general sense that more detail should help. Debugging also works better when it asks whether a problem is global or localized before it asks what's wrong, since a single section drifting needs a localized fix specifically so it doesn't ripple out and drag an otherwise-working song off course.
sections.next: I want to continue improving the efficacy, as each subsequent .md file has taught me how much this aligns with software development principles as well. The goal is still to see how few iterations it takes to achieve the desired sound, so the focus can remain on seeking the most desired performance output.
